ai_explanation.concept_rule: Arc length of a circle of radius $r$ subtending an angle $\theta$ degrees at the center is $s = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r$.
step_by_step: Substitute $s = \pi$ and $r = 3$ into the arc length formula.
Divide by $\pi$ and multiply by 60 to obtain $\theta = 60^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing the arc length formula with the sector area formula.

mark_breakdown.desc: Find the major sector angle: $360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ$ and set up area expression $\frac{300}{360} \times \pi(3)^2$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The area of the major sector is calculated using the reflex central angle $360^\circ - \theta$.
step_by_step: Determine the angle of the shaded region: $360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calculating the area of the unshaded minor sector ($60^\circ$) instead of the shaded major sector.
